name: BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) — county/metro unemployment rate and labor force
gap: The demographics pillar (neighborhood.py) covers population, income, education, and age mix via Census ACS, but has no labor-market/employment signal, and no national series at all exists anywhere in sources.yaml — every current 'development'/'demographics'/'quality' source (dof_sales, development.py, transit.py, livability.py, census_acs for the NYC counties) is NYC-specific, which cuts against the project's stated goal of generalizing to any US neighborhood/property type.
coverage: national — every US county, metro area (CBSA), and many cities
granularity: county and metro (CBSA); NYC-specific use would need a tract-to-county join, same pattern census_acs.py already uses via the tract relationship file
license: US government work, public domain, no restriction.
cost: Free via the BLS Public Data API without a key; a free registration key raises the daily query limit (from 25/day unregistered to 500/day registered) and unlocks bulk multi-series requests — same pattern as the project's existing census_api_key/rentcast_api_key gated sources.
recommendation: Weak recommend, lower priority than fred-mortgage-rate and fhfa-hpi. Employment growth is a textbook leading indicator for housing demand and is genuinely national (unlike most of this project's current demographic/development signals), so it fits the stated gap well. But it would need a new demographics sub-metric and a decision on whether/how it folds into the existing pillar weights, plus the series ID lookup is county-by-county (no single national series ID the way ACS variable codes are) — more adapter complexity than the other two candidates for a less differentiated payoff, since ACS already partially captures economic trajectory via income growth. Worth doing after fred-mortgage-rate and fhfa-hpi, not instead of them.
